brief.headline: Winfred has had a functional decline in bathing and lower-body dressing, with a fear of slipping and skipped showers. His niece and primary caregiver also reports exhaustion and asks for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-11-19 the OT reassessed ADLs. Winfred now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, and he was independent at the last review. The OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing support.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-11-19 OT note: moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-11-14 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting Winfred out of the tub. He said he has been skipping showers because he is afraid of slipping. No fall is documented, and there are no encounters in the period.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-11-14 aide note supports the hands-on help getting out of the tub and the skipped showers from fear of slipping. The encounters record is empty. No fall is documented in the cited note.

items.statement: On 2026-10-25 the niece and primary caregiver (documented as Robert) reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. The notes do not show whether respite was arranged.
items.verifier_note: The 2026-10-25 social work note supports each point: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group. It does not say whether respite was arranged, and the brief says the same.

items.statement: Equipment and home care hours for bathing support were recommended on 2026-11-19. The notes do not show whether the tub transfer bench, handheld shower, or added hours have been ordered or approved. Caregiver strain may affect how the added bathing support can be delivered.
items.verifier_note: The recommendations are in the 2026-11-19 OT note. Neither cited note shows an order or approval. The caregiver strain comes from the 10-25 social work note. Presenting it as something that may affect delivery is a reasonable discussion point and does not assert a fact.

questions_for_team: How quickly can the tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and added home care hours be put in place?
Is there an interim plan for bathing and hygiene while Winfred is avoiding showers?
What respite options can be offered to the caregiver, and when? Who will follow up on evening coverage?
Is a fall-risk or home safety reassessment needed given his fear of slipping and the change in ADLs?
Does the team need to look for a cause of the decline in bathing and dressing ability, given that PCP notes on 2026-10-01, 10-20, and 10-29 describe him as stable?

checks: Confirm review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review date and prior care plan are on file before comparing changes.
Falls and injuries: count falls, near-falls, and fall-related injuries in the window; check for any head injury or fracture, especially given seizure disorder and clopidogrel use (bleeding risk).

Seizure activity: document any seizures, seizure-like events, or rescue medication use; check whether any antiseizure medication is listed. The active medication list shows no antiseizure drug, so reconcile this against the seizure diagnosis with the prescriber and pharmacy records.
ED visits and hospital admissions: list any ED visits or inpatient stays in the window, with reasons (cardiac chest pain, bleeding, hypoglycemia, seizure, falls, back pain).

Medication changes: list starts, stops, and dose changes since last review. Check the four active meds (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin 20 mg) and whether any diabetes medication, antihypertensive, or pain medication appears in claims or outside records but is missing from the active list. Flag simvastatin dose adequacy for ischemic heart disease as a question for the prescriber, not a recommendation.
Diabetes and anemia labs: review most recent HbA1c, glucose readings, hypoglycemia episodes, CBC/hemoglobin trend, and whether results were checked within the expected interval.
Cardiometabolic markers: review blood pressure trend, weight/BMI trend (BMI 30+), lipid panel and triglycerides, and any new chest pain, dyspnea, or angina episodes with nitroglycerin use.
Chronic pain and back pain: check pain scores, analgesic use, and any new opioid or NSAID prescriptions, noting interactions with clopidogrel and renal function labs if available.

Function, ADLs/IADLs, and cognition: compare current ADL/IADL status and any cognitive screen results with the prior review; note any decline that could relate to seizures, pain, or medication effects.

Mood, social engagement, caregiver situation, and care-plan items: screen for depression or mood change, review attendance at PACE center and transport, check caregiver strain and any housing or safety concerns, and confirm care-plan goals and due items (assessments, immunizations, eye/foot/kidney screening for diabetes) are scheduled or completed.
